content: If you are currently taking a combination of reserpine, hydralazine, and hydrochlorothiazide, it is important to contact your doctor to discuss the possibility of switching to an alternative treatment. This medication is prescribed to manage high blood pressure. Reserpine and hydralazine function by relaxing the blood vessels, which facilitates easier blood flow throughout the body. Hydrochlorothiazide helps lower blood pressure by removing excess water and salt from the body. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in tablet form and is typically taken orally twice a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to clarify any part you do not understand. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. This medication helps control high blood pressure but does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, as abruptly discontinuing the medication may lead to increased blood pressure and unwanted side effects. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to reserpine, hydralazine, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some medications and processed foods), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially amitriptyline (Elavil), aspirin, clomipramine (Anafranil), desipramine (Norpramin), digoxin (Lanoxin), doxepin (Adapin, Sinequan), ephedrine, epinephrine, imipramine (Tofranil), indomethacin (Indocin), MAO inhibitors, methylphenidate (Ritalin), metoprolol (Lopressor), nortriptyline (Aventyl, Pamelor), phenylephrine, propranolol (Inderal), protriptyline (Vivactil), quinidine (Quinaglute), trimipramine (Surmontil), and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver or kidney disease, asthma, lupus, gallstones, diabetes, a heart attack, coronary artery disease, rheumatic heart disease, a history of depression, an ulcer, ulcerative colitis, or if you have undergone electric shock therapy. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while taking this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate its side effects. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. Take the medication with meals or a snack. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: dizziness, frequent urination, flushing (a sensation of warmth), headache, loss of appetite, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, eye tearing, stuffy nose, dry mouth, decreased sexual ability, or rash. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: depression, nightmares, fainting, joint pain, muscle weakness or cramps, unexplained fever, yellowing of the skin or eyes, numbness or tingling in the hands or feet, chest pain, swollen ankles, or leg pain. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure monitoring is necessary to evaluate your response to this medication. Weigh yourself daily and inform your doctor if you experience rapid weight gain. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
